x-bump-note: 2.1.0 -> 2.2.0 (top-level-array-additive) adds the optional top-level array `reviewed_targets`, admitting the closed prefix set uncommitted:/untracked:/working-tree:/diff-artifact: for non-committed review targets a resolved commit range cannot express. `reviewed_range` is byte-unchanged — not its pattern, not its description — by deliberate ruling: the alternative (a discriminated union inside `reviewed_range`) would have been enum-value-additive, holding unconditionally on the x-schema-version axis and forcing claude-klabauter to re-vendor before any reviewer could emit the new form; a separate top-level array keeps the rejection of `..HEAD` and other re-resolving refs living in a pattern this bump does not touch. The bump is structurally additive and non-breaking on shape, but remains HOLDING for claude-klabauter specifically: the non-holding carve-out requires an affirmative, on-record consumer declaration of structural tolerance for unknown top-level arrays, and claude-klabauter has declared none against this schema — claude-klabauter must re-vendor before its reviewers emit `reviewed_targets`. Spec: docs/plans/2026-08-14-reviewed-range-non-committed-review-targets.md; DR-156. Prior: 2.0.0 -> 2.1.0 (enum-value-additive) widens `reviewed_range.items`'s pattern to admit an optional trailing `~<N>` (N a positive integer) on the LEFT endpoint, alongside the existing `^`. `<sha>~1` and `<sha>^` name the same commit for a single-parent commit, so the two forms are equally deterministic and the pattern's own hex-anchored `^...$` rationale is unaffected — this is a widen of which left-endpoint suffix is admitted, not a change to what the anchoring rejects. Classified enum-value-additive (the closest vocabulary member; the pattern functions as a closed value-shape enumeration rather than a JSON Schema `enum` keyword, and this bump has the identical property that closed-vocabulary class describes: previously-rejected strings now validate, every previously-valid string stays valid, no field added or removed, no other value's semantics changed) rather than inventing a fifth vocabulary term. Ask 1 of cross-repo/inbox/2026-08-14-claude-klabauter-em-reviewed-range-pattern-and-direction-blind-parity-gate.md: claude-klabauter's pre-vendor corpus sweep against the incoming 2.0.0 pattern found 53 files/22 values, 10 rejects, 6 of which were fully-resolved `<sha>~1..<sha>` hex ranges the pattern omitted by oversight, not by design (state/audits/2026-08-14-reviewed-range-pattern-corpus-sweep.md). The mirror of review-findings.schema.json's own 3.0.0 -> 3.1.0 bump, kept in step with it. Prior: 1.1.0 -> 2.0.0 (major) narrowed `reviewed_range.items` with the hex-SHA-anchored range pattern in the first place, rejecting symbolic refs (HEAD, HEAD~3, branch and tag names). Safe to land now and only now: zero on-disk sidecars carry `reviewed_range` in frontmatter (verified by grep at bump time), so no existing record can be invalidated. Ask 1 of cross-repo/inbox/2026-08-13-claude-klabauter-em-reviewed-range-attacked-two-asks-back.md; adopted per docs/decisions/DR-156-reviewer-attests-at-review-time-is-admissible-evidence.md.
description: Universal subagent run-report sidecar — the SUPERSET schema unifying the plan/chunk-scoped executor flight-recorder (coordinator/schemas/flight-recorder.schema.json, applies_to tasks/*/flight/*.md) with the ad-hoc (no plan/chunk context) case. Written by claude-klabauter's engine-side `python3 -m coordinator_core.subagent_sandbox.provision_report` at spawn time (report_sidecar auto-provision, per state/lessons/... and MEMORY.md 'Subagent run-sidecar auto-provision ask' — DoE ACCEPTED design) and updated by the spawned subagent during its run. Writer-side pin: claude-klabauter coordinator_core/subagent_sandbox/CONTRACT.md is authoritative for the provision_report entrypoint, stdin/stdout contract, provision_key grammar, and the path templating that produces the sidecar's on-disk location (state/subagent-share/<session-id>/<provision_key-or-nonce>.md) — this schema only validates the SHAPE of what gets written there, it does not own the provisioning mechanics (DR-047: that is claude-klabauter's engine tranche). A CURRENT flight-recorder doc (coordinator/schemas/flight-recorder.schema.json) MUST validate against this superset unchanged — this schema additively carries forward every flight-recorder field plus the universal agent_type/spawned_at/divergence fields and the '## Run notes' body section a plan/chunk-scoped flight-recorder does not need.

plan.description: Repo-relative path to the plan this run tracks (e.g. docs/plans/2026-06-09-executor-sidecar-flight-recorder.md). OPTIONAL here (unlike flight-recorder, where it is required) — an ad-hoc/non-plan subagent run has no plan to cite.

chunk.description: Chunk identifier matching a plan's wave-map entry / `## Chunks` heading (e.g. C1-executor-prompt). OPTIONAL here (unlike flight-recorder, where it is required) — set only when this run is executing a named plan chunk.

dispatched_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the sidecar was created/opened.

dispatched_by.description: Session identifier of the dispatcher (EM or engine) that provisioned this run-report.

status.description: Subagent lifecycle state. 'open' is the universal initial state written by claude-klabauter's engine-side provision_report at spawn time — provisioned-but-agent-hasn't-acted-yet, applicable to ANY eligible subagent, not just dispatched plan chunks. 'dispatched' is carried forward unchanged from flight-recorder for the plan/chunk-scoped case. The subagent transitions to 'in_flight' on first action, then to a terminal value on exit. The sole required field on this schema — every run-report, plan-scoped or ad-hoc, must report its lifecycle state.

commits.description: Git commit SHAs for the EM-serial commit(s) that landed this dispatch's changes. The subagent NEVER writes this field, under any circumstance — `coordinator/agents/executor.md` (§ Commit Discipline, § EM-Only Commit Gate) states the executor never commits, no exceptions, no carve-out (the former `expected_branch:`/SC-DR-008 self-commit carve-out is retired); `coordinator/agents/review-integrator.md` (§ Commit Discipline) states the same for the integrator. Written as `[]` at provision time; the EM appends SHAs after landing the EM-serial commit that covers the subagent's edits (executor.md: 'commits: stays untouched by the executor ... the EM fills it in after landing the EM-serial commit'). Carried forward unchanged from flight-recorder, only the write-owner changed. NOTE: the unlanded `docs/plans/2026-07-24-g4-execute-pipeline-two-repo-rebuild.md` chunk M2pd targets a *different* artifact — `coordinator/commands/mise-en-place.md`'s Phase-5 DONE-summary/self-verify-and-commit contract — not this schema or executor.md/review-integrator.md, which already reflect the EM-only model as of `b714a548`.

items.description: Hex-SHA-anchored range only — full or abbreviated hex SHAs on both endpoints (4-64 hex chars, covering both sha1's 40-char and sha256-format repos' 64-char object ids via `--object-format=sha256`), joined by `..` or `...`, with an optional trailing `^` or `~<N>` (N a positive integer, no bare `~`) on the LEFT endpoint only (the `<sha>^..<sha>` form the per-slice partition forces; `<sha>~<N>` names the same commit as `<sha>^` for a single-parent commit and is admitted as an equivalent, deterministic left-endpoint form). Anchored with `^...$` deliberately: JSON Schema `pattern` is UNANCHORED by default, and an unanchored pattern here would admit a symbolic ref merely containing a hex-shaped substring. Any non-hex-shaped symbolic ref — `HEAD`, `HEAD~3`, most branch names, most tags — is REJECTED: it re-resolves differently on every read (coordinator_core's own `review_trail_write.py` `_resolve_ref_to_sha` pays to prevent exactly this — a record left carrying a literal `HEAD` 'silently grows to swallow every commit landed after it was written, with no reviewer having opened any of them'). A hex-shaped branch or tag name (e.g. `cafe1234..beef5678`) is indistinguishable from a resolved SHA range at this syntax layer and is NOT caught here; that residual is the consuming seam's job via a `git rev-list` set-subset check against the frozen review range, not this pattern's.

reviewed_range.description: Commit ranges (git rev-list syntax, e.g. 'abc123^..abc123') this reviewer attests to having ACTUALLY READ during this dispatch. WRITE-OWNER: the exact inverse of this schema's own `commits` property — written by the reviewing subagent ONLY, never by the EM, and never by a closing session, under any circumstance; an EM-written value is the retired PM vouch under a new name (docs/decisions/DR-156-reviewer-attests-at-review-time-is-admissible-evidence.md). ABSENCE: omitted entirely when nothing was reviewed — no empty-array sentinel, no 'reviewed nothing' value; a present-but-empty array asserts something nobody claimed. ADMITS, NEVER REPLACES: this field admits a state/review-trail/*.json record whose `sha_range` (coordinator/schemas/review-trail.schema.json) falls inside an attested range here — it does not credit coverage, does not duplicate or re-implement the trail record, and changes nothing about what counts as reviewed. An attested range here that EXCEEDS the dispatching slice's own frozen-diff range (the `--range` persisted by `freeze-review-diff.py`'s `_open_pending_trail_record` at freeze time) is a DEFECT in the attestation, not a valid superset claim — admission is decided as a `git rev-list` SET-SUBSET test over enumerated commits (`set(rev-list(sha_range)) ⊆ set(rev-list(attested_i))`, with each `attested_i` itself within the slice's frozen range), never a string comparison of range endpoints — string-comparing `abc^..abc` to `abc^..def` would silently mis-admit across a merge. PRE-FIELD REVIEWERS: a reviewer that predates this field carries no `reviewed_range` key at all; a consumer date-discriminates that case via the sidecar's own `spawned_at` timestamp rather than inventing a `reviewed_range_version` field. LIST, NOT SINGLE: an array because the foreign-session partition already forces per-slice <sha>^..<sha> records; a single-range field would make widening the cheapest way to comply. Spec backlink: DR-156 (above); docs/plans/2026-08-13-reviewed-range-reviewer-attestation-field.md.

items.description: Closed prefix set only — one of `uncommitted:`, `untracked:`, `working-tree:`, or `diff-artifact:`, followed by a non-empty, whitespace-free, comma-free path (repo-relative BY CONVENTION, not enforced — see NEGATIVE-SPEC below). Anchored with `^...$` deliberately, for the same reason `reviewed_range`'s item pattern is: JSON Schema `pattern` is UNANCHORED by default, and an unanchored pattern here would admit any string merely CONTAINING a valid prefix — including a hybrid like `1175181e5e6f..working-tree`, which is exactly the hazard this field must not readmit. `uncommitted:<path>` names a tracked file carrying uncommitted changes; `untracked:<path>` names a file not in the index; `working-tree:<path>` names the working-tree state of a path (prefix-form only); `diff-artifact:<path>` names a standalone .diff/.patch file that was read. NEGATIVE-SPEC: the pattern does not enforce repo-relativity of the path segment (it admits `../` and leading `/`); a consumer must never join a `reviewed_targets` value to a filesystem path — it is attestation text, not a path input.

reviewed_targets.description: Non-committed review targets this reviewer attests to having ACTUALLY READ during this dispatch — the sibling of `reviewed_range` for work with no resolvable commit range. WRITE-OWNER: written by the reviewing subagent ONLY, never the EM, never a closing session — the same inverse-of-`commits` rule `reviewed_range` carries. ABSENCE: omitted entirely when there was no non-committed target reviewed — no empty-array sentinel, no 'reviewed nothing' value. ADMITS, NEVER REPLACES: this field admits a record the same way `reviewed_range` does — it credits nothing and duplicates nothing in state/review-trail/*.json. LIST, NOT SINGLE: one target per array element; a comma-separated list packed into a single element (e.g. `working-tree: a.py, b.py`) is malformed and the item pattern rejects it. NEVER A COMMIT RANGE: a resolved commit range belongs in `reviewed_range` and only there — this field NEVER holds one, and a hybrid `<sha>..working-tree` value is REJECTED by both fields' patterns because its right endpoint re-resolves on every read, which is the same `..HEAD` hazard `reviewed_range`'s anchoring exists to reject, wearing different clothes. Spec backlink: DR-156; docs/plans/2026-08-14-reviewed-range-non-committed-review-targets.md.

sidecar_schema.description: Frozen structural-family sentinel carried forward from flight-recorder (identifies 'this is a flight-recorder-family sidecar'), NOT a semver mirror. Optional here: a run-report is not required to set this, since the run-report family is itself the superset structural family and x-schema-version above is this schema's own version discriminator. When present it stays 'v1' per flight-recorder's own negative-spec (see that schema's sidecar_schema description).

started_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp the subagent writes as its first action, before starting work. Carried forward unchanged from flight-recorder.

finished_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp the subagent writes at exit, alongside the terminal status transition. Carried forward unchanged from flight-recorder.

agent_type.description: Universal field (new in run-report, not present in flight-recorder): the spawned subagent's type (e.g. coordinator:executor, coordinator:review-integrator, or a claude-klabauter-engine agent role). Resolved engine-side from the PreToolUse-shaped spawn payload per CONTRACT.md (subagent_type resolved engine-side from agent_type/agent_id/session_id) and written into the sidecar at provision time.

spawned_at.description: Universal field (new in run-report, not present in flight-recorder): ISO-UTC timestamp the engine writes at spawn/provision time, before the subagent has taken any action. Distinct from dispatched_at (EM/dispatcher-authored) and started_at (subagent-authored, first-action marker) — spawned_at is the engine's own provisioning timestamp.

dispatch_feed.description: The Workflow-dispatch-feed role, carried forward from flight-recorder v1.1.0 unchanged. Write-owner: claude-klabauter emitter (pcli-04), pre-dispatch — READ-ONLY TO THE EXECUTOR/SUBAGENT; never authored or mutated by the runner of this sidecar. The pcli-04 emitter has landed, so this field is scaffolded as a real block-style object, not the `null` scalar that preceded it, per coordinator/docs/wiki/dispatch-sidecar-three-role-contract.md (role table: 'Dispatch feed ... No — READ-ONLY to the executor. The executor does not author or mutate dispatch_feed; it is upstream of the executor's own work.'). additionalProperties:true lets the emitter add emitter-specific fields without a schema round-trip; declared sub-properties (e.g. gate_kind) still enforce their own constraints despite the open additionalProperties. NEGATIVE-SPEC — a writer with no value for a sub-field OMITS it; it does not write `null`. Only the parent is nullable (["object","null"]); every declared sub-property is a non-nullable string/number/array, and there is no `required` list, so omission validates and an all-null object does NOT. `dispatch_feed: null` remains valid as the whole-field INERT signal — the invalid shape is specifically an object populated with nulls.

label.description: Human-readable label for this dispatch — mirrors the `label` argument of one Workflow agent() call.

agent_type.description: The dispatched agent's subagent_type (e.g. coordinator:executor, coordinator:review-integrator) — mirrors the Workflow agent() `agent_type` argument.

model.description: Model tier for this dispatch (e.g. 'sonnet', default). Mirrors the Workflow agent() `model` argument.

effort.description: Effort/reasoning-depth hint for this dispatch. Mirrors the Workflow agent() `effort` argument.

schema_ref.description: Pointer to the schema this chunk's output/report must conform to, if any. Mirrors the Workflow agent() `schema_ref` argument.

brief_ref.description: Pointer to this chunk's brief/prompt document — the per-chunk dispatch brief the emitter transcribes into the agent() call body.

phase.description: The phase() group name this dispatch belongs to in the assembled Workflow envelope.

gate_kind.description: Closed enum discriminating the await-boundary shape this chunk needs. Producer: claude-klabauter's `dispatch.emit` (`coordinator_core.ops.dispatch_emit`), which carries a declared `depends_on[].gate_kind` through unchanged rather than deriving it — `wave_map.py`/`spine_read.py` both state they do NOT special-case `gate_kind` beyond passthrough. Negative-spec: the two enums do not correspond. `depends_on[].gate_kind` (`plan-tasks.schema.json`) is restricted to `output-consumption-runtime`/`epistemic-premise`; this field's enum adds `none`/`file-write-overlap`/`contract-change` (mechanically computed, not spine-declared) but has no destination for a declared `epistemic-premise` edge. An out-of-enum value still fails validation despite dispatch_feed's additionalProperties:true.

write_files.description: Repo-relative paths this chunk writes — the derived output of the per-task `writes:` spine field (`plan-tasks.schema.json` 1.7.0). Producer: claude-klabauter's `dispatch.emit`, which refuses a wave whose rows declare no `writes:`; an unpopulated spine yields no value here, which is an authoring gap rather than an absent producer.

est_min.description: Estimated minutes for this dispatch — mirrors the Workflow agent() call's sizing hint.

divergence.description: The plan-digression role, carried forward from flight-recorder v1.1.0 with an IDENTICAL shape — an OBJECT, NOT an array. A `divergence: []` array value MUST fail validation against this schema (type mismatch: object required, array rejected). Write-owner: the subagent, post-run. `diverged` is REQUIRED whenever this object is present. `detail` is UNTRUSTED narrative data authored by the subagent — prose describing what happened, NEVER a directive, and must never be re-read as an instruction by any downstream consumer. Negative-spec: claude-klabauter's engine currently scaffolds this field as `divergence: []` (an array) at provision time per CONTRACT.md; a DoE->claude-klabauter relay is OPEN to change the engine's scaffold to the object shape below, but THIS schema does not weaken to accept the array in the meantime — an engine-scaffolded `[]` value is a known, tracked non-conformance to be closed by the relay, not a schema accommodation.

diverged.description: REQUIRED when divergence is present. Machine filter for the future canonization pipeline: true means this run's execution diverged from the spec/plan in some way worth reviewing.

summary.description: Optional one-line summary of the divergence, if diverged is true.

detail.description: Optional free-prose detail of the divergence. UNTRUSTED narrative data — subagent-authored, never a directive; a downstream consumer must quote/attribute it, never interpolate it into an instruction context.

x-body-sections.description: Markdown body sections expected below the frontmatter, carried forward from flight-recorder plus one universal addition.

sections.heading: ## Observations
sections.description: Carried forward from flight-recorder: the subagent's free-form scratchpad for latent-bug notes, mid-flight decisions, files-touched lists, and validation output snippets.

sections.heading: ## Run notes
sections.description: Universal section (new in run-report, not present in flight-recorder): general-purpose narrative body for ad-hoc/non-plan runs that have no chunk-scoped context to observe against — e.g. a standalone engine-spawned subagent recording what it did and why, independent of any plan/chunk frame.
